gui.grindless.guide.title: Field Guide
gui.grindless.guide.bootstrap.title: Bootstrap
gui.grindless.guide.bootstrap.body: Your Quest Book arrives automatically when you join while your starter kit is unclaimed. If your inventory is full, make one empty slot for delivery. Hold and use the book, select Free starter supplies and press Claim free kit. No crafting or commands are needed: each player can explicitly claim one finite kit of stone, wood, food and basic workshop supplies. Make room for the whole kit; a full inventory rejects the claim without consuming it or dropping items. After claiming, craft a replacement Quest Book if you lose it. Check the current recipes below and keep the materials needed for each build. Construct the Crank Handle, Hand Pump and ceramic workshop, then establish geological collection, bioculture and biomass power. The Crank Handle supplies limited local startup work to eligible F0 process machines; it is not fuel and cannot power the Research Terminal. The Multitool rotates or relocates machines; it never mines. Make glass, copper and redstone through the workshop instead of treating them as required starting supplies. The Hand Crank Dynamo and finite-vein Crude Extractor offer an optional exploration or emergency branch. Ore veins run out, so do not rely on that branch for continuing supply. Make an Atlas when you have its ingredients.
gui.grindless.guide.workshop.title: Ceramic Workshop
gui.grindless.guide.settling.title: Open Settling Line
gui.grindless.guide.settling.body: Place a Settling Channel behind the Settling Trough controller and a Settling Screen behind the channel. Face the line the same way and keep air above its parts; the controller can take a hopper above. Only the controller has item, water and power interfaces. Its current dirt, wet-aggregate and flint-separation recipes are listed below with their quantities. Clay feeds the Mixer and gravel feeds the Quern. Recover eligible output water through a Clay Conduit for reuse; recovery does not create a new source. Flint has no established use in this T0 route. You may keep it as optional stock or discard it normally. Wrong-facing, missing or covered parts pause work without losing the batch. The Multitool rotates parts and the controller reports the exact fault.
gui.grindless.guide.workshop.body: The Quern mills gravel to sand and recovers ceramic grog. A Hand Pump needs a water source in front or below and exports in its facing direction. Feed the Clay Mixer with clay, water and the sand or grog named by its current recipe. Build a 2x2x2 brick chamber with the Firing Chamber controller at the front-left bottom cell and bricks in the other cells. Follow the recipes below for heat, atmosphere, fuel and yields. Reuse grog in the grog-body recipe with fresh clay and water. Insulators support cores, tanks, Clay Conduits, belts and manipulators. Feed the chamber from its free front/left faces and extract below; repairing the structure preserves work. Slag from metal reduction has no established T0 use, and its future usefulness is uncertain. You may discard it normally or keep it if you wish; storage is optional, and no automatic disposal is provided.
gui.grindless.guide.relay.title: Relay Matrix
gui.grindless.guide.relay.body: Make a ceramic Data Core and calibrate it in a powered Research Terminal. The Crank Handle cannot charge that terminal. Finish T0 with the manual five-Relay-Matrix craft using the Calibrated Data Core; the Assembly Bench does not fabricate a Matrix. These Relay Matrices are physical items, not an unlocked permission. The recipes below show current ingredients, yields, time and power. Before relying on the later powered factory, arrange its fuel, water and item handling: owning a Matrix does not power or supply those machines.
gui.grindless.guide.power.title: Voltaic Power
gui.grindless.guide.power.body: Burn charcoal or coal in the Thermal Generator for unattended F1 power. A Flux Pylon MK I covers the first room; it is infrastructure, so it does not consume a Matrix. The Hand Crank stays useful for isolated F0 work, but the factory begins when power reaches the Pulverizer, Arc Furnace, Press and Assembler through the pylon.
gui.grindless.guide.extraction.title: Surveyed Extraction
gui.grindless.guide.extraction.body: Use the Prospector's Scanner before placing a Terrestrial Extractor. A surveyed ChunkVein is finite, but extraction is automated and no longer asks you to hand-mine each unit. Build another outpost when a field runs down; the Factory World has the same surveyed fields beneath its clean grass floor.
gui.grindless.guide.factory.title: First Factory
gui.grindless.guide.factory.body: The Pulverizer turns cobblestone into sand in six seconds. The Arc Furnace vitrifies sand into glass and reduces mineral feed with carbon. The Press makes plates, rods, gears and copper coils with reusable dies. Those parts make the Assembler. Once it exists, feed glass, copper, redstone and a Calibrated Data Core to repeat the five-Matrix batch in twenty seconds.
gui.grindless.guide.renewables.title: Renewable Inputs
gui.grindless.guide.renewables.body: Build continuing supply around Grindless machines: a water-fed Geological Collector supplies aggregate and clay; the Biocultivator uses aggregate, water and daylight to grow biomass; the Biomass Dynamo fuels F0 work from that biomass. Collection needs a geological rock bed in the Overworld or Factory. Culture needs the same dimensions, open sky and enough daylight. Do not assume the line will keep running at night or resume on its own after restarting. The Hand Pump needs a water source in front or below. Mill aggregate for stone and gravel, settle it for mineral feed and redstone, and use biomass for boards, sticks, paper and firing carbon. The formed ceramic workshop makes glass and metals through the recipes below. Reuse grog and recovered water where the recipes allow; replace losses through the pump and source machines. Gathering finite supplies and using vanilla alternatives can help with startup or an emergency. Use this machine loop for continuing supply instead of depending on vanilla cobblestone generators or tree farms. A recipe list does not show whether your own machines have power, water and a suitable site: check their status before relying on the line.
gui.grindless.guide.logistics.title: Logistics and Heat
gui.grindless.guide.logistics.body: Conveyor Belts move items through the first factory; splitters, mergers, sorters and tunnel belts organise the line without power. A Basic Tank and Clay Conduit hold and move ambient water. The Kiln handles low-temperature fired feeds. Use the Process Atlas for exact live recipes and conditions: it describes a route, but leaves the layout decision to you.
gui.grindless.guide.factory_world.title: Factory World
gui.grindless.guide.factory_world.body: After the Assembler can replace consumed matrices, craft a Factory Portal with glass, copper, redstone and one Relay Matrix. It leads to a flat grass construction world at permanent midday, with no weather or hostile spawns. Return through its arrival portal to the exact portal that sent you. Its resource fields remain finite and surveyed, so clean terrain is never free material.
gui.grindless.guide.industrial.title: Industrial Matrix
gui.grindless.guide.industrial.body: T1 ends with a physical F2 Relay Matrix, not a permission. In the Assembler, combine one F1 Relay Matrix, a Machine Casing, four renewable glass and a Flux Cell. The former Matrix is consumed: its relay control is carried forward, the casing is the structure, glass is the dielectric and the cell is the power coupling. This is the hand-off to Industrial; do not expect an F2 machine to be hand-crafted.

gui.grindless.shop.title: Recovery exchange
gui.grindless.shop.subtitle: Trade earned surplus for basic supplies.
gui.grindless.shop.atomic_policy: Pays the full displayed cost and delivers the entire batch together. Main inventory only. Named or tagged payment items are preserved. Nothing is dropped if there is no room.

gui.grindless.shop.detail.stone: The Quern's dry aggregate route yields more stone plus gravel. Use this only for recovery.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.bootstrap_ston: Lost your first supplies? Dig ordinary dirt by hand. This costly restart needs only the already-claimed starter quest, not a working machine.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.bootstrap_wood: Paid restart wood from manually dug dirt. Establish fibreboard production instead of repeatedly digging terrain.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.bootstrap_wate: Lost both starter buckets? Manually dug dirt buys one replacement filled bucket, before any pump or industrial stock. No claim is reset or paid twice.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.gravel: Direct dry aggregate processing also gives cobblestone. This convenience exchange gives no coproducts.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.sand: The Quern makes sand from gravel. Paid convenience does not replace that route.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.clay: Geological collection already supplies clay alongside aggregate. No insulators or finished cores are sold.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.wood: Fibreboard already works as boards in Grindless recipes. Vanilla wood is optional and costs more equivalent boards.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.food: A small food recovery batch paid with real biomass. The original one-time starter food remains unchanged.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.sapling: Optional tree growing and landscaping. The factory's canonical wood substitute is mod-owned fibreboard.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.seeds: Optional farming. No mandatory T0 route depends on growing vanilla crops.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.water: One real empty bucket is consumed and returned filled. No new bucket is created. The Hand Pump remains the normal supply.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.fuel: One emergency charcoal. The Firing Chamber's native biomass-to-charcoal batch is much more efficient.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.bricks: Unlocked after ceramics. Grog remains reusable in ceramic bodies; trading bricks back into grog loses the other payment.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.dirt: For building. Wet aggregate processing gives more dirt per aggregate and also supplies metals and redstone.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.grass: Optional terrain blocks. This does not turn vanilla farming into a mandatory production source.
gui.grindless.shop.detail.glass: Only after physical calibration. You must already have made the first glass and calibrated core yourself.
chat.grindless.shop.book_required: Hold your real Quest Book to open this action. The recovery utility is /grindless shop.

chat.grindless.shop.audit: Recovery economy: %s offers; conservative T0 material certificate=%s; unproved rows=%s. Not a whole-mod or pacing proof.

chat.grindless.telemetry.stopped: Local development telemetry is off. It will not restart automatically.

gui.grindless.quest.chapter_gate: Complete the final T0 task with five valid F1 Relay Matrices to open the T1 chapter.
gui.grindless.quest.no_material_reward: A workshop note, with no item reward.
gui.grindless.quest.objective.read: Read this note and mark it when ready.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson_policy: These workshop notes have no item rewards. Your team's quest progress is shared.
gui.grindless.quest.inventory_not_operat: Before relying on the line, check that it actually produces output.
gui.grindless.quest.live_recipes: Recipes: check JEI or the Process Atlas.
gui.grindless.quest.structure_axes: Plain structure: offsets from the controller are (right, up, back). Rotate every offset with its facing. The controller is at (0, 0, 0).
gui.grindless.quest.guide_migration: Keep your old Guide if you like; the workshop notes now live in FTB Quests. You do not need to hold a Grindless book to use them.
gui.grindless.quest.task.superflat: A flat world, a fresh start
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.starter_suppl: Your first workshop supplies are free rewards in FTB Quests. Make room for all eleven stacks before collecting them; rewards are claimed separately, and items that do not fit may drop on the ground.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.quest_book_he: Open FTB Quests for workshop notes, tasks and rewards; you do not need to hold a Grindless book. Your team shares quest progress, while rewards are collected individually.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.superflat: There is plenty to build with here, even without visible ore: start with the kit, then grow a lasting supply through your workshop. Bedrock works beneath a Geological Collector, while optional extractors read hidden chunk deposits rather than ore blocks.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.construction: Save some stone, boards, sticks, clay and bricks for the machines that will replace them. The Firing Chamber needs brick blocks around its controller, so do not spend the last ones too early.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.multitool: Use your Multitool to rotate machines; sneak-use picks them up with their saved contents and state. It is a wrench, not a pickaxe, and a moved controller needs its structure rebuilt.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.manual_work: Use the Crank Handle on an eligible F0 process machine for %s FU of startup work, with a %s-tick cooldown. Supply its materials and water first; the handle cannot charge a Research Terminal.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.crank: Turn the Hand Crank Dynamo to power a connected F0 machine. This optional generator is separate from the handheld Crank Handle.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.extractor: For an optional early supply, place the Crude Extractor over a compatible hidden chunk deposit and give it F0 power. Deposits run out; use geological collection and the workshop for materials you can keep producing.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.quern: Let the Quern handle the grinding. Sand for the workshop and recovered ceramics are a good place to start.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.water: Put a water source in front of or directly below the Hand Pump; it sends water out through its facing side without power. A source below leaves the output free for a machine or Clay Conduit.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.clay_mixer: Mix your first ceramic bodies, then take them to the Firing Chamber. They will become parts for the rest of your workshop.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.grog: Recover grog from bricks or fired insulators in the Quern and reuse it in the Mixer with fresh clay and water. Keep the insulators you still need for construction; unfired bodies have a separate recovery recipe.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.firing: Build a 2x2x2 chamber with the controller at the front-left bottom corner and brick blocks in the other seven cells, rotating the shape with the controller. Supply carbon fuel and F0 work; the formed chamber handles the recipe's heat and atmosphere.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.ceramics: Fire a batch of insulators and save a few for your next machines. The grog can go back into the Mixer.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.geological_co: Set the Geological Collector on a valid rock bed in the Overworld or Factory World; Superflat bedrock works too. Feed it water and F0 work for aggregate and clay, clearing both outputs.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.aggregate: There is more than one use for aggregate. Keep some aside for construction and biomass while you work on the metal supply.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.settling: Place a Settling Channel behind the controller and a Settling Screen behind that, all facing the same way. Keep air above the channel and screen; repairing the line preserves work already paid for.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.water_recover: Dirt and aggregate settling return some water for reuse through a Clay Conduit, but flint separation returns none. Refill losses from the pump; flint has no T0 use, so keeping it is optional.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.mineral_feed: Settle wet aggregate for redstone and iron or copper mineral feed, then reduce the feed with carbon in the formed Firing Chamber. Slag has no established T0 use and uncertain future value, so keep or discard it as you prefer.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.biocultivator: Give the Biocultivator aggregate, water and F0 work under open sky in the Overworld or Factory World. It needs daylight; check it after a restart and keep a reserve for the night.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.biomass: Before burning the whole pile, set some biomass aside. You will want it when it is time to build again.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.fibreboard: Your own boards, without a tree farm. Fibreboard works in Grindless recipes, but not as a substitute in vanilla plank recipes.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.biomass_dynam: The Biomass Dynamo supplies F0 power: %s FU/t for %s ticks per item. Save some biomass for building and the night.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.fluid_logisti: A Basic Tank buffers ambient water while Clay Conduits carry it between machines. Connect the pump's facing output to an accepting side, and keep hot or incompatible fluids out of this primitive plumbing.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.conveyors: Let the belts do the carrying. Point them toward the next machine and leave yourself a little less to haul.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.workshop_flow: Put a Crude Manipulator between a source and its destination. It can handle the repeated transfers while you build something else.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.assembly_benc: Let the Bench make the workshop's everyday parts. Your first Relay Matrices still need the crafting table.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.research_term: Connect F0 power to the Research Terminal to turn a raw Data Core into a Calibrated Data Core. The handheld Crank Handle cannot charge it; use a working power supply.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.data_core: Make a Data Core from a ceramic insulator and redstone, then take it to a powered Research Terminal. A raw core will not replace the calibrated one in your Matrix craft.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.calibrate: Take the Calibrated Data Core from your powered Research Terminal and save it for the Matrix batch. This quest gives you a Process Atlas, not a replacement core.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.calibrated_co: Keep your Calibrated Data Core safe until you are ready to craft the Matrices. If you lose it, make and calibrate another raw core; claiming a quest again will not replace it.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.relay: Craft five Relay Matrices by hand with a Calibrated Data Core; five valid F1 Matrices complete this milestone and open the T1 chapter. The task does not consume them, and the Assembly Bench cannot make this batch.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1_preview: These later objectives are a look ahead, not part of finishing T0. The T1 campaign is still a work in progress.

gui.grindless.quest.lesson.settling_port: Place a Channel behind the Trough controller and a Screen behind the Channel, all facing the same way, with air above the Channel and Screen. Optional ports access the controller's storage, not their own; repairing the line preserves work already paid for.
gui.grindless.quest.tank_containers: This tank holds %s mB: use a compatible fluid container to fill or drain it, or an empty hand to check its contents. Leave inventory room for exchanged containers; breaking or moving the tank keeps its fluid in the returned tank item.
gui.grindless.quest.ports_limit: Optional substitutions: at most %s ports in this structure.
gui.grindless.quest.ports_bricks: Keep at least %s ordinary brick cells.
gui.grindless.quest.port_slot: Port at (%s, %s, %s): %s; faces for a north-facing controller: %s.
gui.grindless.quest.ports_notes: Ports are optional: rotate their allowed faces with the controller; vertical and unsided access is closed. They share its stock without copying it, and power still enters through the controller.
gui.grindless.quest.t1_development: T1 IN DEVELOPMENT. This is not a finished or accepted campaign, a successful-operation certificate or an activated T2 campaign. Current T1 source, native/client behavior and saved-world compatibility have separate qualification gates.
gui.grindless.quest.path.t1_core: T1 in development - core physical production route
gui.grindless.quest.path.t1_optional: T1 in development - optional branch, not required for the F2 exit
gui.grindless.quest.path.t1_exit: T1 in development - physical F2 boundary, not a T2 unlock
gui.grindless.quest.t1_pylon_limits: Current MK1 limits: supply cube edge %s blocks, automatic link range %s blocks, transfer ceiling %s FU/t. Coverage and transfer capacity do not generate energy.
gui.grindless.quest.t1_non_atlas_route: Implemented route outside the Atlas projection: %s. Use its normal crafting recipe or the machine's fuel interface. No ingredient quantities or cycle duration are inferred here.
gui.grindless.quest.task.forming_dies: Keep dies and form structural parts
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.power.ther: Feed the Thermal Generator with biomass from your T0 base. It supplies %s FU/t while burning. Use JEI for construction, then connect a pylon and power one machine before expanding.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.power.pylo: Place a Flux Pylon MK1 so the generator and machines share coverage. It distributes power; it does not generate any. Check its recipe in JEI and its actual range before adding loads.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.power.firs: Start one powered process and watch its progress. Bootstrap power supplies %s FU/t; Voltaic demand is %s FU/t. Check coverage, fuel, inputs and output space before adding another load. Under-volting slows work, not yield.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.extraction: Build the Prospector's Scanner with JEI and survey a deposit before placing an extractor. Veins are finite. This is an optional mining branch, not the renewable supply your factory needs or a requirement for F2.

Place the Terrestrial Extractor in a surveyed chunk and supply power, storage and an output route. Use JEI for construction. This optional miner draws from a finite vein; keep the mod-owned renewable base running.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.milling.pu: Build a Pulverizer using JEI, then mill mineral feed from your T0 base. Supply power and leave room for its output. Feed the crushed material into the Arc Furnace; ordinary mining remains optional.
Use JEI to build an Arc Furnace and find its reduction recipes. Feed crushed material and carbon, supply power and clear the output. Slag may be discarded; vented carbon monoxide is not stored fuel.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.forming.pr: Build the Press with JEI and fit the matching reusable die. Turn ingots into plates, rods, gears or copper coils for your Assembler. Keep the die in place and leave output room.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.forming.fo: Use JEI to make the Plate, Rod and Gear Dies. The Press keeps these catalysts after each cycle. Form the iron parts for your first Assembler, including its manually crafted Machine Casings.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.forming.co: Make a copper coil in the Press with the reusable Coil Die. JEI shows the recipe. Reserve it for your first Assembler; this T1 route needs no Wire Mill, wire or acid.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.assembly.a: Manually assemble your Assembler with JEI and industrial parts. Automate components or F1 Relay batches when useful; valid manual methods remain available. Normal machines stay manually assembled. Optional Wire Mill expansion is not required for the first F2 Matrix.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.assembly.m: Make replacement F1 Relay Matrices by hand or in the Assembler; JEI shows both methods. Keep calibrated cores supplied from your T0 base. Reserve physical controllers for expansion and the machine-only F2 conversion.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.glass.glas: Keep your T0 renewable base running. Use JEI to follow construction stone through the Pulverizer into sand, then the Arc Furnace into glass. Glass feeds repeated F1 Relay batches and the physical F2 conversion.
Use JEI to build belts and junctions for moving physical items between machines. Match their direction and leave destinations room. This optional transport branch organizes your factory; it is not required for the F2 exit.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.kiln.kiln: Try the optional Kiln branch in JEI: roast feed into oxide, then reduce it in the Arc Furnace. Handle its listed emissions separately. Roasting and later acid processing are not required for F2.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.factory_sp: Reserve core production supplies before building a Factory Portal with JEI. The Factory World offers optional building space, not renewable resources. Your F2 exit does not require a portal or a visit.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.relay_f2.f: Make a Flux Cell by hand or in the Assembler; JEI shows both methods. Choose either route. F2 needs the physical component but does not require stored charge.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.relay_f2.i: Use JEI for the Assembler's F1-to-F2 Relay conversion. Supply a valid F1 Matrix, casing, glass and Flux Cell. Hold the resulting F2 Matrix to complete this objective; no Factory Portal or T2 machine is required.
gui.grindless.quest.lesson.t1.wet_benefi: Acquire a Chemical Washer by manual assembly. It washes crushed feed with water into washed feed and a secondary ingot. Reduce the washed feed in the Arc Furnace. JEI shows recipes; this branch is optional.
chat.grindless.blueprint.invalid_plan: This blueprint contains invalid block data or relative coordinates
chat.grindless.blueprint.outside_world: Blueprint cell is outside the build area: %s %s %s
chat.grindless.blueprint.materials_chang: Building materials changed before construction; try again
chat.grindless.blueprint.interrupted: Stopped after %s of %s blocks. Unused materials returned; the world was not rolled back.
chat.grindless.blueprint.interrupted_unk: Stamp interrupted. Check the world and inventory; an attempted block may remain charged even if a callback failed.
gui.grindless.assembler.title: Assembly target
gui.grindless.assembler.auto_help: Use the legacy input-based choice. Completed paid work keeps its recipe; identical bills may choose another output. Select a named target to avoid ambiguity.
gui.grindless.assembler.held_work: Paid work for this recipe: %s base ticks
gui.grindless.assembler.work_help: Switching stores paid work under its recipe ID. Select that output to resume it. Unavailable work is retained until its exact recipe returns; it never pays another recipe.
gui.grindless.assembler.state.selected: Explicit target. Supply its ingredients, power and output space.
gui.grindless.assembler.state.unavailabl: Target unavailable in the current catalogue. Choose another target or wait for this ID to return. Paid work is retained.
gui.grindless.assembler.state.missing_it: Target waiting for its item ingredients. Check JEI.
gui.grindless.assembler.state.missing_fl: Target waiting for its required fluids.
gui.grindless.assembler.state.conditions: Target waiting for valid process conditions.
gui.grindless.assembler.state.output_blo: Completed work is waiting for output space. No more power is drawn.
gui.grindless.assembler.state.invalid_wo: Invalid saved work is retained, not executed. Repair the saved state before changing targets.
gui.grindless.assembler.result.closed: Selection refused: this machine menu is no longer valid. Reopen it.
gui.grindless.assembler.result.denied: Selection refused: you cannot configure this machine here.
gui.grindless.assembler.result.stale: Selection refused: the target list or menu changed. Use the refreshed list.
gui.grindless.assembler.result.invalid_r: Selection refused: this exact recipe is not available to the Assembler. The previous target is unchanged.
gui.grindless.assembler.result.not_assem: Selection refused: this machine is not an Assembler.
gui.grindless.assembler.result.busy: Selection refused during an active work transaction. Try again.
gui.grindless.assembler.result.invalid_w: Selection refused: invalid saved work is retained and needs repair.
gui.grindless.assembler.result.malformed: Selection refused: invalid request. The previous target and paid work are unchanged.
gui.grindless.assembler.state.work_limit: Stored-work capacity reached. Resume an existing paid target before starting another.
gui.grindless.assembler.result.work_limi: Selection refused: stored-work capacity reached. Resume an existing paid target; no work was discarded.
